principles.status: Feature definitions/crosswalk considered; no positive implementation from a principle mapping alone.

scope_choices: Automated API model review, including a skeptical second-pass synthesis of supplied automated page reviews; no independent human review, replication, code execution or clinical verification.

All 97 supplied text pages were reviewed. Visual observations derive from supplied automated page-image notes; this call had no directly inspectable page images. Direct visual reinspection remains necessary for image-dependent conflicts and scientific interpretation.
The supplied PDF hash and local availability are provenance claims from the source record, not newly computed or filesystem-verified facts.
Feature assertions are intentionally empty at the user's request. This is not a completed 128-feature annotation and must not be admitted as feature-complete without the separate feature pass.
No JSON Schema validator, semantic validation engine, repository access, graph assembly or filesystem write was executed in this call.
SensorWM is an implemented learned healthcare transition method as reported in executed experiments, not a static health-age regressor. Its causal and clinical validity remain separate questions.
Forecast evaluation supplies recorded future actions. Baselines' access to equivalent future-action information is not established, limiting interpretation of comparative forecasting gains.

Decoder-training provenance, its observation-level 15% validation split and separation from the forecasting test set are insufficiently detailed, despite explicit participant-level downstream classifier splits.

The headline average R² does not define feature weighting, exact sample denominator, forecast-step aggregation or uncertainty. Supplementary per-feature results include failures to outperform simple baselines.

Reported 12-week windows, two-state initialization, available 24-week histories and 12-week future coaching plans are different temporal quantities. The exact maximum unobserved forecast span is not fully resolved.
No tolerance-defined effective horizon, quantitative error-versus-horizon validation or clinical horizon enforcement is established.

SIGReg's Gaussian aggregate target, training dropout, repeated evaluation runs and alternative plans do not establish predictive uncertainty, epistemic/aleatoric decomposition or trajectory calibration.
The displacement transition has an absorbing zero-displacement case under the written equations. Its empirical frequency and effects are not tested in the supplied results.

No held-out experimental behavioral intervention or identified individual counterfactual reference validates the alternative-action projections. Authors explicitly acknowledge time-varying confounding.

Historical variability and peaks are proxies for effort and feasibility, not validated current safety, sustainable adherence or joint-action support. The complete candidate grid and all bounds are not supplied.
The 0.1-year minimum projected benefit and behavioral-variability floors are author-selected optimization policies, not independently established clinically meaningful or universally safe thresholds.

CHA combines associations for different endpoints and populations with a mortality-derived age-rate constant. Correlation discounting does not establish an outcome-calibrated joint risk model or causal adjustment.

CHA and mod-LE8 share wearable components. Construct alignment is not wholly independent validation. Optional domains and unadjusted versus collinearity-adjusted CHA require configuration-specific interpretation.
All of Us disease association is a prognostic analysis of existing records; it is not prospective deployment of SensorWM or the coaching system.

All of Us eligibility, informative wear/censoring, recorded-diagnosis timing, daily-minimum-heart-rate proxy and complete-case selection may affect estimates. Causal effects are not established by temporal lag or adjustment for age, sex and BMI.
The complete coaching comparator adds CHA, status-quo projections, ranked options and differing content instructions together. It does not isolate the causal contribution of learned dynamics.

Human ratings reuse 49 profiles and five raters per track. Stated rating-level exact tests and Wilson intervals do not establish independence across cases and raters; human rubric multiplicity handling is incomplete.
The five personas cover 1,079 of 2,780 profiles, not the entire cohort. Recent evaluated snapshots and habitual persona-selection summaries differ, and some eligibility labels require clarification.
Expert-rated anticipated adherence is not actual adherence. Safe-intensity endorsement and plausibility ratings are not adverse-event evidence, noninferiority, effectiveness or authorization.
Rater heterogeneity is substantial. A claim of uniform adherence-preference direction conflicts with one coach's reported 44.9% Counterfactual win rate.
Reported failures include redundant steps for already active users, ambiguous incremental-step wording, overly optimistic adaptation timescales and nonzero unfavorable safety/plausibility ratings.

Several downstream tasks and subgroups lose discrimination. Small positive counts, broad confidence intervals and absent multiplicity/equivalence protocols preclude broad preservation or fairness guarantees.
Supplied visual notes report larger correlation discrepancies than the manuscript's qualitative narrative suggests. Direct image confirmation is required before a definitive image-based conclusion.
The thyroid-medication subgroup P-value differs between supplied text and the supplied visual-review note. Both values are retained pending direct-source verification.

Automated plan evaluation uses the same named primary model family as generation, supplies model projections as legitimate judging context, and exhibits ceiling effects. It is not independent human or clinical corroboration.
The prompts suppress model/simulation terminology while requesting exact payoffs. Appropriate uncertainty communication and reliance calibration are not established.
No prospective silent use, intervention trial, realized patient benefit, actual-care safety evaluation or regulated deployment is established for the reported coaching system.

Code is promised upon publication, not verified released. Model weights, asset licenses, executable configurations, training compute and latency are not reported sufficiently. Private Fitbit data limit reproducibility.
The reported WCG protocol applies to the described pretraining data use; it does not independently establish approval scope for every cohort, expert activity or future clinical deployment.
Cited systems, commercial age products and methodological references were read as bibliography/source content, not independently retrieved and not used to inherit capabilities.
